root_cause.text: `panthor_fw_unplug()` in the Panthor DRM firmware teardown path unconditionally tried to halt and wait for the MCU even when the firmware/MCU state was not initialized, so the halt/wait code could dereference a NULL firmware pointer during unplug.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `panthor_fw_halt_mcu(ptdev);` and `panthor_fw_wait_mcu_halted(ptdev)` from `drivers/gpu/drm/panthor/panthor_fw.c`, and the commit message states that “the FW may not even be loaded/initialized at all, the latter of which can lead to a NULL pointer dereference.”

vuln_statements.content: drm_warn(&ptdev->base, "Failed to halt MCU on unplug");

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify the firmware unplug path by removing the explicit MCU halt and wait sequence before stopping the firmware.
intent_record.what: Removed the calls to panthor_fw_halt_mcu() and panthor_fw_wait_mcu_halted(), along with the associated DRM warning, from panthor_fw_unplug() so that the function now goes directly from suspending the IRQ to panthor_fw_stop().
intent_record.how: At runtime, firmware unplug no longer attempts to explicitly halt the MCU or wait for it to report a halted state during this shutdown path. The unplug sequence becomes shorter and avoids the halt/wait step, leaving firmware stop as the remaining teardown action.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional MCU halt call in the unplug path is the direct trigger for dereferencing firmware/MCU state even when it was never initialized.
This wait-for-halt check follows the halt request and would also operate on uninitialized firmware state, contributing to the NULL firmware pointer dereference during unplug.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 51407254986501b19681d55531963f1ea58e89cd
Author: Karunika Choo <karunika.choo@arm.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 25 12:55:46 2025 +0000

    drm/panthor: Support GLB_REQ.STATE field for Mali-G1 GPUs
    
    Add support for the GLB_REQ.STATE field introduced in CSF v4.1+, which
    replaces the HALT bit to provide finer control over the MCU state. This
    change implements basic handling for transitioning the MCU between
    ACTIVE and HALT states on Mali-G1 GPUs.
    
    The update introduces ne
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present here in the buggy form; this function body adds explicit MCU halt handling and checks around unplug. In particular, `panthor_fw_unplug()` now does `panthor_fw_halt_mcu(ptdev);` followed by `if (!panthor_fw_wait_mcu_halted(ptdev)) drm_warn(...)`, which means it no longer unconditionally waits without a halt request. The helper `panthor_fw_mcu_halted()` also gates GLB_STATE usage with `if (panthor_fw_has_glb_state(ptdev))`, and `panthor_fw_has_glb_state()` itself reads the interface version from `panthor_fw_get_glb_iface(ptdev)`. Since the shown code already contains the added halt/wait sequencing and timeout handling, the vulnerable unconditional teardown logic is not present in this snippet and the fix is already included.

Author: Karunika Choo <karunika.choo@arm.com>

    Add support for the GLB_REQ.STATE field introduced in CSF v4.1+, which

    ACTIVE and HALT states on Mali-G1 GPUs.
    
    The update introduces ne
bic_trace_step.reason:
The vulnerable construct described is an unconditional halt/wait on unplug that can run when firmware/MCU state is not initialized. In this snippet, `panthor_fw_unplug()` now explicitly does:

- `panthor_fw_halt_mcu(ptdev);`
- `if (!panthor_fw_wait_mcu_halted(ptdev)) drm_warn(...);`

and the helper `panthor_fw_wait_mcu_halted()` is guarded by `panthor_fw_mcu_halted()`, which reads MCU status and, when supported, GLB state: `halted = gpu_read(ptdev, MCU_STATUS) == MCU_STATUS_HALT;` and `halted &= (GLB_STATE_GET(glb_iface->output->ack) == GLB_STATE_HALT);`. This is not an unconditional dereference of a NULL firmware pointer in the unplug path as described; the shown code also indicates the new controlled halt/wait logic was introduced as the fix. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is present.
